llm.summary: This skill is not clearly malicious, but it gives an agent paid and persistent account-level authority that is broader and less tightly confirmed than a narrow mobile Listing optimizer should have.

dimensions.detail: Network access to https://ari.funewa.com, Bearer authentication, account checks, billing balance queries, report downloads, and local export writes are expected for this service. The every-session check retrieves user, balance, and auto-confirm policy even for potentially narrow read-only requests, which is broader than strictly necessary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses a browser authorization flow or manual hidden API-key entry and stores the key under ~/.ari/config.json with 0600-style permissions. This is disclosed and purpose-aligned, with no observed remote code download or dependency install, but it does persist a service credential locally.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly allow server-side auto-confirmed paid generation without a fresh user approval, tell the agent not to ask again when autoConfirm is returned, and accept minimal confirmation for some paid flows. The final fixed-workflow section requires listing/mobile, but the included CLI accepts workflow/focus overrides for operations commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can change persistent account behavior through autoconfirm settings, recurring collection schedules, watch state, competitor bindings, alert read state, and workbench review status. These actions are mostly disclosed, but auto-confirm and recurring collection can create future costs or account-state changes with compressed user confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is mobile Listing diagnosis with fixed listing/mobile defaults, but the package also exposes broad ARI account operations: paid VOC and other analyses, collection, monitoring, competitors, exports, alerts, workbench status updates, and category tools. Much of this is disclosed and related to Amazon review operations, but it exceeds the narrow advertised surface.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving this skill access to your ARI account, saved local API-key credentials, paid analysis workflows, and persistent account settings. Before using it, consider setting ARI to ask before every paid action, use “只报价，不执行” when you only want pricing, and review any request that changes monitoring, competitors, exports, workbench status, or autoconfirm rules.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The package does use shell-driven CLI execution, network requests, environment/config API-key lookup, local credential storage, and export file writes. These capabilities are disclosed in the artifact and coherent with ARI integration, so this is transparency guidance rather than a standalone malicious signal.
[TP4] unexpected: The broad ARI command set is present in the skill text and CLI. Many commands are related to Amazon review/listing operations, but the breadth is larger than the narrow mobile Listing optimizer description and creates a real scoping concern.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The natural-language entry can cover generic review analysis, while the skill also supports paid and state-changing workflows. The artifact includes some safeguards, but the trigger surface is broad for the authority exposed.
[EA2] unexpected: The repeated autoConfirm findings are supported by SKILL.md, reference.md, and ari.py: voc/analyze can execute and deduct credits when server autoConfirm is true, and the instructions tell the agent not to seek fresh confirmation afterward. This is not malware, but it is a material user-control concern.
[T05] unexpected: The SARIF workflow/focus override concern is supported by scripts/ari.py: operation_payload gives command-line workflow/focus values precedence over skill-defaults.json, despite the specialized artifact saying listing/mobile is fixed.
[T05] expected: The mandatory check does retrieve user, balance, and autoConfirm information each session. This is authenticated service metadata rather than credential exfiltration, but it is broader account data than a minimal mobile Listing read-only task requires.
